slides.headline: He was born in a Punjab village. In 2026, he became the first Australian to win horticulture's top global honor.
Prof. Zora Singh won the American Society for Horticultural Science's 2026 Outstanding International Horticulturist Award
slides.body: Born in village Aitiana, Ludhiana, Punjab, on August 10, 1956, he earned his BSc, MSc and PhD at Punjab Agricultural University before a postdoc in the UK and a move to Australia in the 1990s.

slides.headline: Now Foundation Professor of Horticultural Science at Edith Cowan University, he's spent over three decades researching fruit shelf life and quality.
slides.body: The ASHS award is described as the field's highest global honor - and he's the first Australian ever to receive it, after a career built entirely on a Punjab Agricultural University education.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat benefits when an agricultural science degree from Ludhiana becomes the foundation for a field-defining global career.
slides.body: Singh's path - from a Punjab village to Australia's top horticulture chair - shows how far an Indian agricultural science education can carry someone who takes it seriously.
